Department of Neurobiology & Biophysics

Brain-wide circuits for perception, cognition and action

We record from thousands of neurons across the whole mouse brain at once — with Neuropixels electrophysiology, cortex-wide calcium imaging, and optogenetics — to work out how distributed circuits turn sensation into decisions.

Behind this text: 141 neurons recorded simultaneously, 90 s of a real Neuropixels recording from this lab. Each mark is one spike; rows are sorted by depth along the probe.

What we do

Four ways of watching a brain make a decision

No single method sees enough. We combine dense electrophysiology, mesoscale imaging, causal manipulation, and quantifiable mouse behavior on the same questions — and build the tools when they don't exist yet.

Live · widefield

Widefield calcium imaging

Activity across the entire dorsal cortex at 35 frames per second. This panel is a real recording, rebuilt in your browser from its SVD components.

Neuropixels

Brain-wide electrophysiology

Hundreds of neurons per probe, many probes at once, spanning cortex to midbrain. We help build the Neuropixels ecosystem and the International Brain Laboratory's brain-wide map.

Visual cortex

Vision and visual decisions

Retinotopic maps, receptive fields, and psychophysics in mice trained on two-alternative visual discrimination — behavior precise enough to model.

Circuits

Causal circuit dissection

Optogenetics plus anatomy: which projections actually carry a signal, and what happens to behavior when we silence them.

Cortex, live

Twenty-six seconds of mouse cortex

A real widefield calcium recording, running continuously — both hemispheres of dorsal cortex at 35 frames per second. Warm is activity above the session mean, dark is below.

Subject ZYE_0092, 2 June 2025. The whole camera field of view, 900 frames reconstructed live from 8 spatial components — a few hundred KB instead of a video file. The trace below the image is mean fluorescence across the frame.

Lab news

April 2026

Jordan's midbrain paper is out in Neuron

The midbrain reticular formation turns out to carry the context signal that decides which rule a mouse applies to the same visual stimulus.

2026

Contingency degradation, in Nature

A collaboration with the Stuber lab tracking prefrontal → VTA dynamics as mice learn that their actions no longer matter.

2026

A review of where large-scale electrophysiology is going

Josh Siegle and Nick take stock of single-spike-resolution recording in Nature Reviews Neuroscience.

Open science

Take our data. Take our code.

Everything below is public. If a tool you need doesn't exist, tell us — we probably want it too.

Datasets

  • Neuropixels Ultra waveforms — browse or download
  • Olfactory Pavlovian conditioning — ephys + 2P
  • Neuropixels 2.0 with imposed brain motion
  • Visual discrimination recordings — also in NWB and ONE

Software

  • Pinpoint — plan probe insertions
  • Kilosort2 — spike sorting at scale
  • allenCCF — work with the Allen atlas
  • widefield — analyse imaging data
  • Alyx — experiment database

Hardware & how-to

  • Neuropixels wiki and user forum
  • Wheel task — designs and code
  • Surgical protocols — cranial windows and implants
